sources.entry: Antigravity Link - VS Code extension that bridges mobile devices to Google's Antigravity IDE (a Claude-powered VS Code fork). Mirror active AI chat sessions on your phone, send messages, upload files, stop AI generation, and automate workflows via a local HTTP API or 9 MCP tools. Listed in the official MCP Registry.

summary.one_liner: A VS Code extension that mirrors an Antigravity IDE chat to a phone browser over the local network and exposes a local HTTP API and MCP server to drive the session.
summary.what_it_does: Antigravity Link runs a local HTTP or HTTPS bridge server from inside VS Code and discovers Antigravity windows through the Chrome DevTools Protocol on a remote debugging port. Scanning a QR code opens a mobile web UI that shows the active chat as it streams, lets you send messages, stop generation, upload files, and use voice-to-text. It supports switching between multiple Antigravity windows. For automation, it provides REST endpoints such as /snapshot, /send, /stop, /upload, and /click, all protected by a bearer token, plus an MCP server (mcp-server.mjs) with nine tools. The README says the server is LAN-only by default and the UI is available in 16 languages.
use_cases: monitor an AI coding session from my phone
send follow-up messages to an IDE chat remotely
upload files into an Antigravity chat from mobile
stop AI generation from a phone
drive IDE chat sessions from scripts via HTTP API
let an AI assistant control Antigravity through MCP tools
how_to_run: Launch Antigravity with --remote-debugging-port=9000 (every window must be launched this way)
In VS Code, run the command 'Antigravity Link: Start Server'
Run 'Antigravity Link: Show QR Code' and scan the code with your phone
Accept the self-signed certificate warning in the phone browser
For MCP: add the node command with args pointing to mcp-server.mjs in the installed extension folder, with AG_BRIDGE_URL and AG_BRIDGE_TOKEN set
notable: Mobile mirror of a live Antigravity chat, with a dedicated stop control and voice input
Nine MCP tools plus a documented REST API with bearer-token auth
Discovers sessions via Chrome DevTools Protocol, without modifying Antigravity files
Self-signed local HTTPS by default for microphone access
Interface localized into 16 languages with RTL support for Arabic
caveats: Requires Antigravity to be launched with a remote debugging flag; sessions started without it are not discovered
Server is LAN-only by default; remote access needs an external tunnel the README mentions only generally
Phone and computer must be on the same Wi-Fi network
keywords: send messages to ai from phone
